source.title: Why to "grow" and "harvest" deep learning models?

record.tranche_reason: The experiments compare held-out accuracy for sigmoid models trained with SGD, Adam, and AdaGrad, but do not directly measure the training–test gap or the conditions in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy curves comparing optimizers and LIGHT activations. The text says LIGHT-V and LIGHT-G outperform the default adaptive and non-adaptive methods on the test subsets, but does not state a direct Adam-versus-SGD result. Figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The sigmoid-SGD, sigmoid-Adam and sigmoid-AdaGrad baselines compare held-out accuracy with the same activation, including on image datasets, and therefore bear on V4. However, the supplied text preserves neither readable curve values nor an explicit baseline optimizer ranking, so it cannot establish a directional verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim LIGHT improves transparency, convergence and inductive bias through balanced predefined growth and harvesting rates without overparameterization. The explicit claim of outperforming all evaluated baselines appears in the synthetic-results discussion; the experimental-dataset discussion describes configuration dependence, including cases favoring harvesting alone.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a modified output activation (LIGHT) and compares its test accuracy with default sigmoid activations using SGD, Adam, and AdaGrad. It does not reproduce the original claim's experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across datasets, network architectures, and LIGHT configurations; the paper describes some experimental datasets as favoring the -E- configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report improved test accuracy and convergence for SGD with LIGHT activations relative to default sigmoid baselines. This comparison changes the activation as well as the optimizer, and LIGHT hyperparameters receive a search while baseline optimizers use defaults.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the output activation to LIGHT with balanced growth and harvesting parameters can improve convergence and held-out accuracy relative to default sigmoid-based training.

record.problems: Optimizer-comparison values are presented in figures without recoverable numbers in the supplied text. The reported optimizer defaults and mini-batch size are stated, but there is no direct textual Adam-versus-SGD test-accuracy result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the relevant optimizer curves are figure-only in the supplied text, and no direct Adam-versus-SGD outcome is stated. The paper's LIGHT-versus-baseline result does not isolate the optimizer comparison named in V4.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or comparison with natural-label generalization.
Synthetic-data width sweeps do not establish zero training error, training to convergence, or behavior beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or test of local connectivity.

No language benchmarks, learning-rate or decay-schedule tuning comparison, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching. Training performance is not reported alongside the test curves to assess the training-performance qualification.
Batch size is fixed at 75; no batch-size or recipe-adaptation comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or comparison of generalization-gap rankings.
No identification or removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The figure-only optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not added to missing. Their unreadability warrants withholding verdicts, not labeling V4 absent or limited. V4 concerns held-out performance and does not require an explicit training–test-gap measurement. The image-data sampling descriptions conflict: Section 5.2 describes an 80/20 split of 1,000 samples, whereas Appendix D describes 1,000 training and 200 test examples.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep reports test error beyond the interpolation threshold.

The paper compares sigmoid-SGD, sigmoid-Adam, and sigmoid-AdaGrad on test accuracy, but gives no extractable optimizer-to-optimizer values or explicit Adam-versus-SGD result. Language benchmarks, equal or better training performance, and tuning conditions in the version are not tested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
